reason: Conversation 2 gave the right first steps in one efficient turn (unplug, drum by hand, belt, brushes, listen, read the door label), hedged its diagnosis appropriately, told the owner to match brushes to the motor make (Sole/Welling/Ceset) rather than just the machine model, added sensible commutator and connector-scorch checks, and set a clear escalation point if new brushes don't restore drive. Conversation 1 reached the same brush diagnosis but led with the belt as 'most common', issued a 'stop using this appliance' banner for a faint one-off smell weeks ago (over-escalation per the ground truth) and then contradicted it by saying 'plug the machine back in', declared 'that confirms it' when armature/module faults can't be excluded, and gave no plan if the new brushes don't fix it.
